A1.justification: Both 12-page PDFs describe the same TEAM research and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables. Both end with references; neither contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original TEAM evaluations on SDAR 30B-A3B, including benchmark performance, component ablations, and design analyses.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, and design analyses, including the results in Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same delayed caching, speculative exploration, and limited expert activation procedures. Algorithm 1 is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HumanEval and MBPP code generation and GSM8K and Math-500 mathematical reasoning. No dataset, task, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains vanilla SDAR as the baseline, and Table 3 retains Refresh-4, Refresh-8, and Refresh-free. The newly cited work is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Table 1 retain zero-shot SDAR 30B-A3B evaluation, block size 32, acceptance threshold 0.95, the same hot-token settings, four branches, and identical metrics and procedures.

E4.justification: The component ablation, hot-token sensitivity study, cache-refresh comparison, candidate-acceptance analysis, and hidden-state similarity analysis are unchanged in Figures 5–6 and Tables 2–4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figures 1–6 retain identical results and findings. For example, Table 1 reports the same 2.20× HumanEval speedup and 1.94× average speedup in both versions.

T1.justification: The decoding equations (1–3), hot-token definition (4), and associated mathematical reasoning are unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty claim, three complementary TEAM strategies, and claim of up to 2.2× acceleration with negligible performance degradation.

C2.justification: The explanations involving routing consistency, cache stability, memory-bound inference, and candidate alignment are unchanged. Section 5.1 also retains the qualification concerning unavailable LLaDA 2.0 evaluation tooling.

D1.justification: The A100 80GB hardware, implementation and hyperparameter disclosures, and code-release link remain identical. No reproducibility or resource-access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Yan et al. (2026b), 'Pixel-space diffusion transformers,' as background on diffusion generative modeling. The existing Yan et al. (2026) reference is retained as 2026a; research positioning is otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: The preprint date changes from May 25 to August 4, 2026, alongside updated arXiv version/date text and citation suffixes. The prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added citation causes paragraph reflow on page 2 and bibliography reflow across pages 11–12. All figures, tables, and Algorithm 1 retain their displays and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 adds one background citation and makes minor date and layout updates. The citation supplies no new analysis or comparison, while the methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and substantive explanations remain unchanged. These edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
